issues.item: Rumination: Revenge: ruminate about how to get even with assailant
issues.explanation: The revenge-focused rumination is hard to reconcile with this patient’s trauma context and role. A 63-year-old refugee aid worker exposed to terrorism may plausibly have anger, but specifically ruminating about how to get even with an identifiable assailant is clinically strained in terrorism trauma, where perpetrators are often anonymous, inaccessible, or deceased. A clinician would question whether this item fits the same trauma narrative as the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Fear of Rage: I will not be able to control my anger and will do something terrible
issues.explanation: These two items together imply a strong retaliatory/violent action focus (revenge planning plus fear of acting on rage), but the rest of the profile centers on dissociation/disorganized memory and fear-based appraisals rather than a coherent anger-driven PTSD presentation. This makes the profile internally uneven in a way that is difficult to explain as one formulation.

issues.item: Rumination: Revenge: ruminate about how to get even with assailant
issues.explanation: Revenge-focused rumination is hard to reconcile with this patient's trauma context as a refugee aid worker exposed to terrorism; it implies an identifiable personal assailant against whom retaliation is contemplated, which does not fit well with the rest of the profile and is not supported by the memory/appraisal content.

issues.item: Hypervigilance: I have to be on guard all the time
issues.explanation: Hypervigilance is misclassified under Negative Appraisals and reads more like an ongoing current-threat state. In this formulation, Threat is inactive and there are no Threat items provided; this item therefore sits awkwardly with the node structure and weakens coherence of the selected appraisal items.
